info.name: Iam-hero bridge
info.description:
Every endpoint the Iam-hero PC bridge serves, in the order a happy path uses them.

**Set two things and nothing else:**

1. `baseUrl` — `http://127.0.0.1:8765` on the PC itself, or the Tailscale Funnel address (`https://<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net`) from anywhere else.
2. `deviceToken` — leave it empty. Run **Pairing → Confirm pairing** once and its test script stores the returned token here for every other request.

`profileId`, `storyId`, `jobId` and `illustrationId` are filled in the same way by the requests that produce them, so the collection runs top to bottom without copy-paste: **Management → List profiles** fills `profileId` the first time it finds one and never overwrites a value you typed yourself.

**Management → Delete profile everywhere is irreversible** and takes that child's whole shelf with it. Read the folder rather than running it end to end.

Authentication is set once at the collection level as `Bearer {{deviceToken}}`. `GET /health` and the two pairing endpoints opt out of it, exactly as the bridge does.

All errors use the typed envelope `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`. Every request's description names the codes it can answer with. Full documentation: `bridge/README.md`.

Nothing in this file is real: no token, no child's name beyond the README's own example, no library path.

variable.description: Bridge address. Loopback on the PC; the Tailscale Funnel https address from anywhere else.
Filled automatically by Confirm pairing. Never commit a real one.
Set by hand: another device's id from List devices, never the caller's own.
Filled by Management → List profiles when empty, or set by hand. Never commit a real one.
Filled automatically by Read sync manifest.
Filled automatically by Queue story generation and Queue illustrations.
Filled automatically by Read sync manifest.

item.name: Health
item.description: The one endpoint that answers before pairing. Ask it first whenever anything looks wrong.

item.name: Pairing
item.description: Human-in-the-loop, by design: the 6-digit code is printed on the PC console and never travels over HTTP. Codes expire after 2 minutes, live in memory as hashes only, and five wrong attempts invalidate the pending pairing.

request.description:
No auth. Prints `Pairing code: XXXXXX — expires in 2 minutes` on the **PC console** and answers `201`:

```json
{ "pairingId": "b6c1..." }
```

Copy the `pairingId` into the next request, and read the code off the PC screen. The code itself is never sent over HTTP and only its SHA-256 digest is kept, in memory.

Errors: `429 rate_limited` beyond 5 pending requests per rolling minute.

exec: pm.test('a device token came back and was stored', function () {

request.description:
No auth. Registers the device and answers `200` with a one-time 256-bit token:

```json
{ "deviceToken": "..." }
```

**The test script stores that token in the `deviceToken` collection variable**, which is what every other request in this collection authenticates with. The bridge cannot hand it out again, so if you clear the variable you must pair afresh.

Errors: `404 pairing_not_found`, `410 pairing_expired`, `403 invalid_pairing_code`. **Five wrong attempts invalidate the pending pairing** — after that even the correct code fails and you need a new Request pairing.

item.name: Devices
item.description: The paired-device registry. Names and dates only; tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and are never listed.

request.description:
Requires auth. Lists paired devices that can still authenticate, marking the caller's own row:

```json
{ "devices": [ { "id": "...", "name": "Family tablet", "createdAtUtc": "2026-08-22T10:00:00Z", "lastSeenAtUtc": "2026-09-04T09:12:00Z", "isCaller": true } ] }
```

`lastSeenAtUtc` is null for a device that has never called since pairing. This is the cheapest way to prove `deviceToken` works: every endpoint except `/health` and the two pairing endpoints answers `401 unauthorized` without a valid bearer token.

Requires auth. Set `deviceId` from the list above (any row whose `isCaller` is false). Removes that device's token, so its very next call answers `401 unauthorized` and the family member pairs again with a new code when wanted. Answers `200`:

```json
{ "id": "...", "removed": true }
```

Errors: `409 cannot_remove_self` (a device may not remove itself, so the parent can never lock themselves out), `404 device_not_found` (unknown or already removed), `401 unauthorized`.

item.name: Management
item.description: What the owner can see and remove without opening the app: who is in the master library, what has been written for them, one whole book, and the one irreversible delete. Read-only except the last request. No photo bytes are ever returned, no page prose appears in a listing, and nothing in this folder is written to a log.

request.description:
Requires auth. Every child the master library knows, oldest first:

```json
{
  "profiles": [
    {
      "id": "profile-1",
      "displayName": "Nour",
      "hasPhoto": true,
      "storyCount": 3,
      "createdAtUtc": "2026-08-22T10:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAtUtc": "2026-09-01T18:20:00.000Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

**The test script fills `profileId`** the first time it finds one, and never overwrites a value you set yourself — so the Profiles folder below works without reading a sync manifest first.

`hasPhoto` is a yes-or-no: no endpoint ever returns the photo bytes or its path. There is no age here — the bridge stores no birth date, and the age a story was written for travels in the generation request without being kept.

Errors: `401 unauthorized`.

query.description: Optional. Enable to list one child's shelf instead of the whole library.

request.description:
Requires auth. Every story with its illustration progress, oldest first:

```json
{
  "stories": [
    {
      "id": "…",
      "profileId": "profile-1",
      "title": "Nour and the Sea Lanterns",
      "languageCode": "ar",
      "pageCount": 6,
      "illustrations": { "pending": 1, "completed": 4, "failed": 1 },
      "createdAtUtc": "2026-08-22T10:04:11.000Z",
      "updatedAtUtc": "2026-08-22T10:31:02.000Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

Titles only — page prose lives one request down. The three illustration counts always add up to the story's illustration rows, so `pending` covers anything not yet drawn and not failed.

The `profileId` query parameter ships **disabled**; enable it to list one child's shelf. A value naming no profile answers `400 invalid_field` naming the parameter rather than an empty list, so a typo can never read as "this child has no books". Any other query parameter is refused the same way, by name.

Errors: `400 invalid_field`, `401 unauthorized`.

Requires auth. The whole book — every page's prose, its English scene description, and its illustration id and status:

```json
{
  "story": {
    "id": "…",
    "profileId": "profile-1",
    "title": "Nour and the Sea Lanterns",
    "languageCode": "ar",
    "createdAtUtc": "2026-08-22T10:04:11.000Z",
    "updatedAtUtc": "2026-08-22T10:31:02.000Z",
    "pages": [
      {
        "id": "…",
        "pageNumber": 1,
        "text": "…",
        "illustrationScene": "…",
        "illustrationId": "…",
        "illustrationRelativePath": "illustrations/<storyId>/0.png",
        "illustrationStatus": "completed"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Byte for byte the answer **Sync → Download story** gives a paired device: one serializer and one shape, so the owner never reads a story in a form the family's devices do not.

`storyId` is filled by **Sync → Read sync manifest**, or copy one from List stories above.

Errors: `404 story_not_found` (which is also the answer for a deleted story), `401 unauthorized`.

Requires auth. **Irreversible, and it takes the child's whole shelf with it.** Removes the profile row, every story it owns, every page, every illustration row, the rendered image files and the reference photo. The rows go in one transaction, so either all of them go or none do:

```json
{
  "profileId": "profile-1",
  "deletedAtUtc": "2026-09-03T09:12:44.000Z",
  "deletedStoryCount": 3,
  "deletedPageCount": 18,
  "deletedIllustrationCount": 18,
  "removedFileCount": 15,
  "photoRemoved": true
}
```

`removedFileCount` counts files actually deleted from disk, which is lower than `deletedIllustrationCount` whenever some pages were never drawn.

One `deletion_records` entry is written **per deleted story** — the same record a single story delete writes — so a paired device that never saw this happen learns each book is gone from its next sync manifest, through the path it already understands. The profile's own disappearance needs no record: a manifest carries the complete profile list, so a child no longer in it is a child who is gone.

Unlike deleting a story, this is **not** idempotent: nothing records that a profile once existed, so a second call is indistinguishable from a mistyped id and answers `404 profile_not_found` — the same typed error the photo endpoints answer for an unknown child.

Errors: `404 profile_not_found`, `401 unauthorized`.

item.name: Profiles
item.description: What the PC knows about one child: the reference photo — the one thing that makes the hero look like the same child on every page — the hero sheet the PC reads out of it, and how that child's name is written in each story language. Set `profileId` by hand before using the requests that name one. The photo bytes never leave the library: they are not logged, not echoed, and never sent to a paired device, only to the local ComfyUI while a page renders. The sheet does leave, but only to a paired device that asked for one named child, and never into a log or a sync manifest.

header.description: image/jpeg or image/png only (image/jpg is accepted for the former).

request.description:
Requires auth. **The body is the image itself, not JSON** — pick the file under Body → binary, and set `Content-Type` to match it.

```text
PUT /profiles/profile-1/photo
Authorization: Bearer <deviceToken>
Content-Type: image/jpeg

<raw bytes>
```

Answers `200`:

```json
{
  "profileId": "profile-1",
  "relativePath": "photos/profile-1.png",
  "contentType": "image/png",
  "sizeBytes": 148213
}
```

The declared type is a claim and the bytes are the evidence: the file must start with that format's magic bytes. For the best likeness use a clear, front-facing, well-lit head-and-shoulders photo — the portrait pass sees one centre-cropped 512x512 square.

Errors: `400 unsupported_image_type` (wrong or missing `Content-Type`), `400 invalid_image` (bytes that are not that format, or an empty body), `413 photo_too_large` (over 2 MB), `404 profile_not_found`, `401 unauthorized`.

Requires auth. Removes the photo and answers `200`:

```json
{ "profileId": "profile-1", "removed": true }
```

Idempotent: a profile that has no photo answers `200` with `"removed": false`. Pages rendered afterwards simply stop resembling anyone in particular.

Errors: `404 profile_not_found`, `401 unauthorized`.

Requires auth. How this child's hero is **drawn**: the three traits the PC read from the reference photo, the outfit and prop the hero always has, and the hash of the photo the first three came from.

```json
{
  "profileId": "profile-1",
  "sheet": {
    "hair": "short curly black hair",
    "skinTone": "warm brown",
    "eyeColor": "dark brown",
    "outfit": "wearing a red knitted cardigan over a white collared shirt",
    "prop": "carrying a small brass lantern",
    "photoHash": "9f2c…",
    "updatedAtUtc": "2026-09-03T20:14:02.000Z"
  }
}
```

A child whose photo has never been read answers `200` with `"sheet": null` — a state, not a failure. A sheet may also hold only an outfit and a prop, with the three derived values empty, when a parent typed a wardrobe before any photo reached the PC.

Errors: `404 profile_not_found`, `401 unauthorized`.

item.name: Set what the hero wears and carries

request.description:
Requires auth. Writes the half of the sheet the **parent** owns and nothing else: `outfit` and `prop`. The three derived values are the PC's, read from the photo, and cannot be set here — `hair`, `skinTone`, `eyeColor` and `photoHash` are refused as unknown fields.

Both fields are optional and both may be blank, which clears them. Each is at most 80 characters, because the line they join is repeated into every page's scene description.

Answers `200` with the same body *Read hero sheet* returns. A profile whose photo has never been read still gets its wardrobe stored; the derived half fills in the first time a photo is read.

Errors: `400 invalid_field` (an unknown field, or one over the length limit), `404 profile_not_found`, `401 unauthorized`.

Requires auth. Reads the child's stored reference photo again and rewrites the three derived traits, **ignoring the photo-hash cache** — that is the whole point of the request. The outfit and the prop are never touched.

Answers `202` with `"started": true` and the sheet as it stands by the time the PC answers:

```json
{
  "profileId": "profile-1",
  "started": true,
  "sheet": { "hair": "long straight brown hair", "…": "…" }
}
```

The re-read takes its turn at the one GPU gate like a story or a render does, so a card that is busy drawing a book keeps it and the sheet in the answer is still the old one; ask again, or read the sheet, once the PC is free. Nothing here fails: a profile with no photo, an Ollama that is down and a model that answered in the wrong shape all leave whatever was already stored.

Errors: `404 profile_not_found`, `401 unauthorized`.

Requires auth. Asks the story model how one child's given name is written in each of the four story languages, and answers `200`:

```json
{
  "spellings": {
    "ar": "مليكة",
    "en": "Malika",
    "sv": "Malika",
    "so": "Maliika"
  }
}
```

One Ollama call with a JSON schema, on the **story** model (`ollamaModel`), taking its turn at the same GPU gate as generation and rendering. Its budget is 15 seconds — the whole request is capped at 20 — because a parent is waiting in the profile editor for the answer. A cold model on a busy card will miss that; asking again once it is resident is cheap, and the parent may always type the four spellings by hand.

Names no profile and writes nothing: this is a suggestion about a string, and the device decides whose profile it belongs to. The name is never written to a log line, here or anywhere else.

`heroName` is required (≤ 60 characters). `gender` is optional, `girl` or `boy`, and only refines the wording — leave it out and the prompt says nothing about it.

All four values come back or none do: an answer that is not four names in the right scripts is refused whole. The spelling then travels back on `POST /stories/generate` as `heroNameSpelling`.

Errors: `400 invalid_field`, `400 invalid_json`, `401 unauthorized`, `503 ollama_unavailable` (unreachable, too slow, or an answer that was not four names).

item.name: Stories
item.description: Writing a book. One job at a time behind a single worker, because the PC has one 4 GB GPU; jobs live in memory and a bridge restart clears in-flight work.

exec: pm.test('the job was queued and its id was stored', function () {

body.raw:
{
  "profileId": "profile-1",
  "heroName": "Nour",
  "heroNameSpelling": "نور",
  "ageYears": 6,
  "genderContext": "girl",
  "languageCode": "ar",
  "theme": "A lantern festival by the sea",
  "moral": "Sharing a small light makes it bigger",
  "pageCount": 6,
  "illustrationStyle": "pictureBook",
  "favoriteTopics": "sea turtles and paper boats",
  "recurringWorld": "the Lantern Harbour"
}

request.description:
Requires auth. Queues one story generation job and answers `202` — nothing has been written yet:

```json
{ "jobId": "…", "queuePosition": 1 }
```

**The test script stores `jobId`**, so Read story job below polls this job with no copy-paste. Position `1` means next or already starting.

`profileId`, `heroName`, `ageYears`, `genderContext`, `languageCode`, `theme`, `moral`, `pageCount` and `illustrationStyle` are required. `genderContext` is `girl` or `boy`, `languageCode` is `ar`, `en`, `sv` or `so`, `pageCount` is `6`, `8` or `10`, and `illustrationStyle` is `pictureBook`, `watercolor` or `colorful3d`. `favoriteTopics` and `recurringWorld` are optional (≤ 240 characters each); absent, `null` and blank all mean the same thing and the prompt then says nothing about them.

`heroNameSpelling` is optional (≤ 60 characters) and is **how the family writes this child's name in `languageCode`** — `مليكة` for an Arabic book, `Malika` for an English one; see **Profiles → Suggest name spellings**. Given one, both prompts use it and forbid any other spelling of the name in the answer, and the language check stops tolerating letters of another script at all — the tolerance only ever existed for a name the model had no way to write. Absent, `null` and blank all mean the same thing and the story is written with `heroName` exactly as before.

Errors: `400 invalid_field` (before a job exists), `400 invalid_json`, `401 unauthorized`, `413 body_too_large`. Failures reported later on the job itself: `ollama_unavailable`, `ollama_timeout`, `invalid_model_output`, `library_write_failed`, `cancelled`, `internal_error`.

Requires auth. Polls one job:

```json
{
  "jobId": "…",
  "status": "generating",
  "progress": "Writing the story (attempt 1 of 3).",
  "createdAtUtc": "2026-08-22T10:00:00.000Z",
  "updatedAtUtc": "2026-08-22T10:00:04.000Z"
}
```

Statuses run `queued → generating → validating → completed`, or `failed` / `cancelled`. `queuePosition` is present only while `queued`; a failed job carries `"error": {"code": …}`; a completed one carries the whole book under `story`, with one `pending` illustration row per page. A ten-page story can take several minutes on the 4 GB card — poll, do not assume.

The generation request is never echoed back: it holds the child's name.

Errors: `404 job_not_found` — which is also the answer for a job another device created, so ids cannot be probed. `401 unauthorized`.

Requires auth. No body. Idempotent; answers `200` with the status the job ended in:

```json
{ "jobId": "…", "status": "cancelled" }
```

A queued job leaves the line immediately. A running job has its in-flight request to Ollama aborted and is never persisted — cancelling always means "no story", never "half a story".

Errors: `404 job_not_found`, `401 unauthorized`.

Requires auth. No body. **Permanent, with no undo** — the recovery path for a mistake is a backup. Deletes the pages, the illustration rows and the illustration files, and records the deletion so every other device drops its copy too.

```json
{
  "storyId": "…",
  "alreadyDeleted": false,
  "deletedAtUtc": "2026-08-22T10:05:00.000Z",
  "removedFileCount": 6
}
```

Idempotent: a story that is already gone answers `200` with `"alreadyDeleted": true` and the original deletion time. Profiles and reference photos are never touched. Removing one device's offline copy is a different thing and calls no endpoint at all.

Errors: `404 story_not_found` (an id that was never in this library), `401 unauthorized`.

item.name: Illustrations
item.description: Drawing the pages. The illustration and story queues share one GPU lock: while a page renders no story is written, and vice versa. The lock is taken per page, so a story queued behind a ten-page book waits for one page, not ten.

exec: pm.test('the render job was queued and its id was stored', function () {

request.description:
Requires auth. Queues rendering of every page that has no image yet — `pending` and `failed` rows both count, `completed` ones are skipped — and answers `202`:

```json
{ "jobId": "…", "pageCount": 6, "queuePosition": 1 }
```

**The test script stores `jobId`**, so Read illustration job polls this job directly. `pageCount` is how many pages *this job* renders, not how long the story is: after a run where one page failed, a second call answers `"pageCount": 1`.

The body is optional and carries the two things the library does not remember about a story but a picture needs. An absent `illustrationStyle` falls back to `pictureBook`; an absent `genderContext` leaves the hero described as a child.

Errors: `400 invalid_field` (a present-but-invalid value), `404 story_not_found`, `401 unauthorized`. Failures reported later on the job: `comfyui_unavailable`, `comfyui_timeout`, `comfyui_failed`, `invalid_image_output`, `image_write_failed`, `library_write_failed`, `missing_custom_node`, `cancelled`, `internal_error`.

Requires auth. Polls one illustration job:

```json
{
  "jobId": "…",
  "storyId": "…",
  "status": "rendering",
  "progress": "Rendering page 3 of 6.",
  "pageCount": 6,
  "completedPageCount": 2,
  "failedPageCount": 0,
  "createdAtUtc": "2026-08-22T10:00:00.000Z",
  "updatedAtUtc": "2026-08-22T10:04:12.000Z"
}
```

**A `completed` job may still have failed pages** — read the counts, not the status. `failed` means no image landed at all. `queuePosition` is present only while `queued`. Nothing in this payload is story content: no scene descriptions, no prompts, no file paths.

Errors: `404 job_not_found` (including a job another device created), `401 unauthorized`.

Requires auth. No body. Idempotent; answers `200` with the status the job ended in:

```json
{ "jobId": "…", "status": "cancelled" }
```

A queued job leaves the line immediately. A running job **stops after the page it is currently rendering** — that page is finished and stored, and no page after it is started. Throwing away a nearly finished minute of GPU work would help nobody.

Errors: `404 job_not_found`, `401 unauthorized`.

item.name: Sync
item.description: Manifest → downloads → complete. There is deliberately no change feed: one manifest of metadata plus timestamps is smaller and far harder to get wrong than a cursor a device could lose or replay.

exec: // Prefer a completed illustration: only those can be downloaded.

request.description:
Requires auth. The complete story: title, language, and ordered pages with the prose, the English scene description, and each illustration's id, path and status. Exactly the payload shape a completed generation job returns, so a device parses one format either way.

```json
{
  "story": {
    "id": "…",
    "profileId": "profile-1",
    "title": "…",
    "languageCode": "ar",
    "createdAtUtc": "…",
    "updatedAtUtc": "…",
    "pages": [
      {
        "id": "…",
        "pageNumber": 1,
        "text": "…",
        "illustrationScene": "…",
        "illustrationId": "…",
        "illustrationRelativePath": "illustrations/<storyId>/0.png",
        "illustrationStatus": "pending"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Call it only for stories whose manifest `updatedAtUtc` is newer than the copy you hold.

Errors: `404 story_not_found` — including a story that was deleted. `401 unauthorized`.

header.description: Send back the ETag you stored last time to get 304 instead of the image.

request.description:
Requires auth. **The one endpoint that answers with bytes instead of JSON**: the rendered page as `image/png`, with a strong `ETag` (the SHA-256 of the file contents) and `Cache-Control: private, no-cache`.

Enable the `If-None-Match` header above with a stored tag to get `304 Not Modified` instead of the image. A content hash rather than size-and-mtime, deliberately: a re-render writes the same path with a new timestamp, and re-downloading a byte-identical image on every sync is exactly what the tag exists to prevent.

Two response headers carry the page's identity so you need not join back to the manifest: `x-illustration-story-id` and `x-illustration-page-number`.

Errors stay typed JSON: `404 illustration_not_found` (unknown id), `409 illustration_not_ready` (the row is not `completed` — a different thing from a missing story, and a row claiming `completed` while its file is gone reads as `409` too), `401 unauthorized`.

Requires auth. Send the `generatedAtUtc` of the manifest this device finished applying. Upserts one `sync_state` row for the calling device inside a transaction and answers `200` with the stored value:

```json
{ "deviceId": "…", "lastSyncedAtUtc": "2026-08-22T10:00:00.000Z" }
```

The watermark is the manifest's own generation time, not the time this report arrived, so anything written while the device was downloading is simply picked up by the next sync.

Errors: `400 invalid_field` (missing or unparsable timestamp), `400 invalid_json`, `401 unauthorized`.

item.name: Backup
item.description: Encrypted snapshots of the whole master library. The file itself never travels over HTTP — only its name does. It is written into the library's own `exports/` folder, so copy the `.ihmb` file somewhere else yourself: a backup that exists only on the PC it backs up protects against a mistake but not against a dead disk.

request.description:
Requires auth. Writes one AES-256-GCM encrypted snapshot (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 200 000 iterations, random salt and nonce) into the library's `exports/` folder and answers `201`:

```json
{
  "fileName": "iam-hero-master-20260822T101530Z.ihmb",
  "sizeBytes": 184913,
  "createdAtUtc": "2026-08-22T10:15:30.000Z",
  "rowCount": 47,
  "fileCount": 12
}
```

It holds every database row plus every file under `photos/` and `illustrations/`. **Device token hashes are never in a backup** — a backup that could authenticate a device would be a credential, and this one is a document. `exports/` is excluded, so backups never nest.

Errors: `backup_password_too_short`, `backup_too_large`, `backup_write_failed`, `401 unauthorized`.

Requires auth. Copy the `.ihmb` file back into the library's `exports/` folder first, then name it here. Replaces the library with that file's contents and answers `200`:

```json
{
  "fileName": "iam-hero-master-20260822T101530Z.ihmb",
  "backupCreatedAtUtc": "2026-08-22T10:15:30.000Z",
  "restoredRowCount": 47,
  "restoredFileCount": 12,
  "restoredDeviceCount": 2,
  "devicesMustRePair": true
}
```

**After a restore every device must pair again**, including the one that asked for the restore: restored device rows exist so the parent recognizes the list, but they cannot authenticate anything. So this collection's `deviceToken` stops working the moment this succeeds.

Restore is all-or-nothing: the file is authenticated, decrypted and fully validated before anything is touched, and the database is refilled inside one transaction. A wrong password, a flipped bit, a foreign file or a payload this build cannot read all fail before any change.

Errors: `backup_password_too_short`, `backup_invalid_file_name`, `backup_not_found`, `backup_unreadable`, `backup_authentication_failed` (wrong password **or** an altered file), `backup_unsupported_version`, `backup_too_large`, `backup_restore_failed` (the one non-atomic window: a file-system failure with the database already restored), `401 unauthorized`.
